To: docs/climate-programme/border-revenues-launch/handover
Replying to: none
Cc: none
Subject: DRAFT — Thursday launch handover for Inês

Inês,

I’m so sorry to leave you with this so late, especially after finding the error this afternoon. My father is ill, and I’m with my family. I don’t know yet how long I’ll be away, so please plan on leading Thursday’s launch without me.

I trust you completely to do this. You know the paper as well as I do, and you ran the Annex B sensitivity work yourself. I’ve set out the practical things in order below, but please use your judgement where plans need to change. And thank you for taking this on.

1. Correct the public materials first

The 2030 LDC-relevant revenue estimate in Figure 3 and the summary came from the old run, before the free-allocation phase-out was applied. The correct number is EUR 1.4 billion, not EUR 2.1 billion. The conclusion of the paper does not change, but the headline number does.

PDF v7 on the drive is already corrected on pages 3, 14 and 15. Please use that as the version of record, and check any copies or links being prepared for publication point to v7.

The remaining corrections are:

- Deck v4: update slides 6 and 9, including the chart on slide 9 and any speaker notes or spoken headline that still say 2.1. Please do a quick check of the rest of the deck for the old figure too.
- Press release: Hanna’s embargoed release went to 34 Brussels contacts on Friday with the incorrect figure. Please contact her first thing and make sure a corrected release goes to everyone who received it, with the correction clearly identified, before the embargo lifts at 10:00 CET on Thursday. Ask her to confirm when this is done. Geert knows I’m away and can sign off the corrected release if she needs a senior name.

This mistake is mine, not yours. If anyone asks how it happened or whose error it was, please say so. There is no need to soften or obscure the correction: the old run was used in the figure and summary; the corrected estimate is 1.4 billion; the paper’s conclusion remains the same.

2. Settle the press calls

Hanna told two journalists I would be available Wednesday afternoon. The calendar has background calls at 14:00 and 15:00, 20 minutes each, with Hanna to confirm. Please speak to her about whether you can take them and ask her to confirm the arrangements with both journalists. Make sure they have the corrected number and PDF v7 before the calls. If you can’t take either call, please agree an alternative with Hanna rather than leaving the expectation that I will join.

3. Confirm the event and security arrangements

Tomás sent a change this morning that supersedes the timing in the run of show. Please confirm the revised plan with him:

- Guests should still be at the security entrance by 12:00; Tomás is collecting badges. He needs the final names from our side by Wednesday at 12:00 at the latest, or security will not let them in. Please send him your name and the names of anyone else attending from our side, and confirm receipt.
- Light lunch is outside the room from 12:00.
- Lindqvist welcomes everyone at 12:30 for five minutes.
- Your presentation starts at 12:35 and should be 15 minutes, not 20.
- The panel starts at 12:50. Lindqvist has to leave at 13:30 and wants to take at least two questions herself before she goes.

Please ask Tomás how he and Lindqvist want to handle the remaining moderation, audience questions and close after 13:30. The old run of show has Q&A at 13:40 and close at 14:00, so we need an agreed revised running order rather than assuming it still works. Please also confirm that you are replacing me for both the presentation and panel.

Abena is joining remotely. Her link is in the calendar invite; she tested it last week. It would still be worth checking with Tomás who is managing the connection and sound on the day, and making sure Abena has the revised timing and corrected paper.

4. Presentation and panel

Please make the presentation your own. The corrected deck is the starting point, not a script. Lead with the paper’s main finding and what it means for LDCs, using the 1.4 billion figure. Fifteen minutes will go quickly, so leave space for the argument rather than trying to cover every slide.

Kessler has said he will challenge the 80% pass-through assumption and raise resource shuffling. Don’t let him set the tone of the whole discussion. Acknowledge the concern, explain the evidence and bring the conversation back to the paper’s wider question: who pays at the border and what the revenues mean for LDCs.

On pass-through, 80% is the central case. Annex B also tests 60% and 40%: the result holds at 60% and weakens at 40%. Say that openly, without getting defensive. You know those runs better than anyone. On resource shuffling, we agree it is a risk; it is covered in section 5.2, and we recommend the Commission’s monitoring report. Abena may also want to speak to the LDC perspective, but please don’t rely on her to make our argument for us.

And remember Lisbon: when the projector died at the COP side event, you rescued my panel. You’re better live than you think.

5. After the event

Lucy Tran will attend with a colleague. For the Halvorsen grant report, she has asked for two event photos and attendance numbers, ideally by 4 December. Please agree with someone on the day who will take the photos and record the number, and send them to Lucy afterwards or make sure there is a named person to do it.

You can call me if you need me. After 9:00 tomorrow I may not pick up, though, so please don’t hold a decision waiting for me. For anything that needs senior sign-off, go to Geert.

I’m sorry again for the extra work and the short notice. Thank you for carrying this through. I have every confidence in you.

Marieke
